questions.solution:
Let $P(n): 4^n+15 n-1$ is divisible by 9 .
For $n=1, P(1)=4^1+15 \times 1-1=18$, which is divisible by 9 .
$\therefore P(1)$ is true.
Let $P(k)$ be true. Then, $4^k+15 k-1$ is divisible by 9 .
$\Rightarrow 4^k+15 k-1=9 \lambda$, for some $\lambda \in N$.
We shall now show that $P(k+1)$ is true. For this, we have to show that $4^{k+1}+15(k+1)-1$ is divisible by 9 .
Now, $4^{k+1}+15(k+1)-1=4^k \cdot 4+15(k+1)-1 \begin{aligned}& =(9 \lambda-15 k+1) \times4+15(k+1)-1 \\
& =36 \lambda-45 k+18 \\
& =9(4 \lambda-5 k+2), \text{ which is divisible by }9 .
\end{aligned} $\therefore P(k+1)$ is true.
Thus, $P(k)$ is true $\Rightarrow P(k+1)$ is true. Hence, by PMI, $P(n)$ is true for all $n \in N$.$

The binomial expansion of ${\left(a + b\right)}^{n} = C0 n {a}^{n}{b}^{0} + C1 n {a}^{n - 1}{b}^{1} + C2 n {a}^{n - 2}{b}^{2} + . . . + Cn n {a}^{0}{b}^{n}$ and to find the sum of coefficients of all the powers of $x,$ put $x = 1,$ in the expansion.

Hence, the sum of coefficients of all the powers of $x,$ in ${\left(3x - 1\right)}^{15}$

is ${\left(3 \times 1 - 1\right)}^{15} = {2}^{15} .

Also, the sum$ of coefficients of all the powers of x,$ in ${$\left(1 + x\right)$}^{15}$ is ${$\left(1 + 1\right)$}^{15} = {2}^{15} .

Also, the sum$ of coefficients of all the powers of x,$ in ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{16}$ is ${\left(1 + 1\right)}^{16} = {2}^{16}$ and in ${\left(1 - x\right)}^{16}$ is ${\left(1 - 1\right)}^{16} = 0 .

We know that ${$\left(a + b\right)$}^{n} + {$\left(a - b\right)$}^{n} = 2 $\left[C0 n {a}^{n}{b}^{0} + C2 n {a}^{n - 2}{b}^{2} + C4 n {a}^{n - 4}{b}^{4} + . . .\right]$ and

${\left(a + b\right)$}^{n} - {$\left(a - b\right)}^{n} = 2\left[C1 n {a}^{n - 1}b + C3 n {a}^{n - 3}{b}^{3} + C5 n {a}^{n - 5}{b}^{5} + . . .\right] .

Hence, ${$\left(1 + x\right)}^{16} + {\left(1 - x\right)}^{16} = 2 \left[C0 16 + C2 16 {x}^{2} + C4 16 {x}^{4} + . . . + C16 16 {x}^{16}\right] and

${$\left(1 + x\right)$}^{16} - {$\left(1 - x\right)$}^{16} = 2 $\left[C1 16 x + C3 16 {x}^{3} + C5 16 {x}^{5} + . . . + C15 16 {x}^{15}\right]$ .

But $r = 0, 1, 2, . . . , 15,$ hence the sum of coefficients of all the powers of $x,$ in ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{16} + {\left(1 - x\right)}^{16}$ is $\dfrac{{2}^{16} + 0}{2} - C16 16 = {2}^{15} - 1$ and in ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{16} - {\left(1 - x\right)}^{16}$ is $\dfrac{{2}^{16} - 0}{2} = {2}^{15} .

Hence,$ the sum of coefficients of {x}^{r}, $\left(r = 0, 1, 2, . . . , 15\right)$ in the expansion of ${\left(3x - 1\right)}^{15}$ is same as the sum of the binomial coefficients of ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{15}$ and ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{16} - {\left(1 - x\right)}^{16}$ i.e. $\left(a\right)$ and $\left(c\right)$ only.
